messages:
Miguel Ramos: Hey people-ops — quick heads up. I moved my primary residence from NJ to NY on 2025-09-15 and updated Workday, but my last two paystubs (payrun 2025-09-30 and 2025-10-15) still show NJ state withholding and there's a municipal tax line for Newark. Also noticed the W-2 mailing address is my old NJ address. Can we update the withholding residency retroactively and make sure the W-2 gets mailed to my NY address? Thanks.

Anna Chen: @Miguel Ramos thanks for flagging. Can you confirm the exact date you changed your address in Workday and attach a screenshot of the current home address field? I can kick this over to payroll after that. :+1:

Miguel Ramos: I changed it on 2025-09-15 and I have the Workday confirmation email. attaching screenshot now (uploaded).

Jake Patel: looping in payroll. @Anna Chen @Miguel Ramos we can do two things: 1) update the state allocation moving forward, 2) run a payroll retro adjustment to correct state/municipal withholding for affected payruns, or 3) if retro is small we can leave as-is and handle on tax return. Which do you prefer? Also we will need Miguel's employee ID and last 4 of SSN to pull the payrun.

Miguel Ramos: Employee ID 82746, last4 4321. I'd prefer the retro adjustment if it's straightforward — I want withholdings to reflect NY residency for the pay period after 9/15.

Lucy (tax): FYI — moving from NJ to NY midyear can change both state and local withholdings. If payroll issues corrected amounts after year-end, payroll may need to issue a Form W-2c (corrected W-2) if totals change materially. We usually try to correct via payroll adjustments first.

Jake Patel: Thanks. I pulled the payruns. There's a municipal code applied because the old address triggered Newark local tax. We'll: 1) update the work address in payroll system to Miguel's NY address, 2) submit retro adjustment for 2025-09-30 and 2025-10-15 to zero out Newark local and move the state withholding to NY rates for those payruns, 3) confirm totals and only issue W-2c if box totals change after adjustments.

Anna Chen: Miguel — I'll update your mailing address for year-end forms now and note this thread. Expect an email when payroll completes the retro. Please confirm whether you want us to hold physical mailing until you confirm the new address (we can forward but not ideal for sensitive docs).

Miguel Ramos: Please mail to my NY address (same as Workday) — no forwarding. I updated Workday already but want confirmation that Payroll updated the address too.

Jake Patel: Got it. Running adjustment job now (job id: adj-2025-82746-01). Command I ran: 
```
payroll-cli retro-adjust --emp 82746 --runs 2025-09-30,2025-10-15 --remove-local NJ-NEWARK --apply-state NY --note "midyear residency update"
```
Will post when complete.

payroll-bot: Retro adjustment job adj-2025-82746-01 queued. ETA ~15m.

Sarah O'Connor: Quick benefits note — moving states can affect state tax benefits like NJ sick leave accruals. Miguel, if you have state-specific benefit questions ping me and I'll verify changes to accruals/eligibility.

Jake Patel: adj-2025-82746-01 completed. Results: NJ local tax removed, state withholding reallocated to NY for those payruns. Net pay changed by -$12.34 total (refund to company or small recalc depending on year-to-date). I updated mailing address for W-2s to the NY address on file. No W-2c required (box totals unchanged aside from local line) — closing unless you want a physical confirmation.

Miguel Ramos: Awesome, thank you all. Can I get a one-line confirmation email for my records?

Anna Chen: Yep — I'll send a confirmation email to you summarizing the adjustments and new W-2 mailing address. :email:

Miguel Ramos: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround! :raised_hands:
